figure.name: Joseph Stalin
figure.role: Soviet leader associated with party-state consolidation, central planning, industrialization, coercive institutions, and wartime leadership.
figure.hook: Stalin = Soviet state consolidation, industrialization, repression, and the party-state model.
whyHere: Stalin belongs here because the study guide has to examine how a revolutionary state became a centralized party-state with planning, security institutions, industrialization, and limited dissent.

He matters because many political arguments use Stalin as shorthand for socialism or communism. The page needs to identify the specific Soviet party-state model instead of turning every public program into Stalinism.
figure.cleanIdea: Stalin's road is about Soviet state consolidation: party authority, planning, industrial policy, security institutions, and constrained dissent.

hallCard.timelineMeaning: The Soviet system centralizes party authority, planning, industrial policy, security institutions, and limits on dissent.

ideas.title: Party-State
ideas.plainDefinition: A party-state is a political system where the ruling party and state institutions are closely fused.
ideas.context: In the Stalin path, party-state means party authority shapes administration, planning, security institutions, and public political life.
ideas.whyMatters: Party-state matters because it names a specific political structure instead of using socialism as a vague insult.

ideas.title: Central Planning
ideas.plainDefinition: Central planning means major production, investment, and distribution decisions are directed through state planning institutions instead of mainly through private market decisions.
ideas.context: In the Stalin path, planning is tied to rapid industrialization, state targets, and administrative command.
ideas.whyMatters: Central planning matters because it is a specific economic institution, not the same thing as any tax-funded public service.

ideas.title: Stalinism
ideas.plainDefinition: Stalinism names the Soviet political model associated with centralized party leadership, state planning, coercive institutions, and limited dissent under Stalin.
ideas.context: In the Stalin path, Stalinism is a historical party-state model, not a synonym for every form of socialism or public spending.
ideas.whyMatters: Stalinism matters because it keeps the page precise: public roads, public schools, welfare states, and Soviet party-state rule are not the same category.
